application.name: TSDF Reconstruction
application.description: Dense 3D reconstruction on the GPU with holoscan-tsdf: a synthetic RGB-D camera circles a known tabletop scene with known poses, TsdfIntegrateOp integrates every frame into a TSDF volume, and TsdfMeshOp ray casts the volume from each pose and extracts its mesh every N frames. Every ray cast is checked against the scene's exact depth and every mesh against its exact surfaces, and HoloViz shows the input depth beside the shaded ray cast.

changelog.1.0.0: Initial release: the holoscan-tsdf demo, with a synthetic RGB-D camera, ground-truth reporters, a HoloViz view and a PLY export.

hardware.name: NVIDIA GPU
hardware.description: A CUDA-capable GPU supported by the Holoscan SDK, with about 300 MiB free for the default 256^3 volume and its mesh.

synthetic.description: Reconstruct the tabletop scene over two orbits (240 frames at 640x480 into a 256^3 volume), meshing every 30 frames, check each ray cast and mesh against the truth, and show the depth and the ray cast when a display is available.

ci.description: Finite headless check: one orbit of 60 synthetic 640x480 frames into a 256^3 volume, meshing every 20 frames; every ray cast's depth error and coverage and every mesh's vertex error against the scene's exact surfaces.
